items.item: The day view lists rooms as rows, each labelled with its capacity (and its floor or equipment), against a time axis that covers working hours and is labelled at least every hour
items.evidence: renderDayView() (page.html:221-285) lays rooms out as COLUMNS (`roomColumns += '<div class="flex-1 min-w-[150px]...'`), each with capacity/floor/equipment in a column header, while time runs vertically down each column via `hourLabels` (8 AM–6 PM, labelled every hour). Capacity/floor/equipment and an hourly-labelled axis covering working hours are present, but rooms are not laid out as rows against a horizontal time axis as required — orientation is inverted (room-per-column grid, confirmed by audit.json rows:{single:0,double:0,multi:0}).

items.item: A Day / Week switch marks the active view (aria-pressed, aria-selected or aria-current), Previous / Today / Next controls move the range, and a heading states the date or date range on screen (such as "Mon 2 – Sun 8 Nov 2026")
items.evidence: dayBtn/weekBtn (page.html:38-39) only toggle Tailwind classes via viewBtnClass() (page.html:168-170, 174-175) — no aria-pressed/aria-selected/aria-current attribute is ever set (grep for aria- in the file returns no matches). Previous/Today/Next (#prevBtn/#todayBtn/#nextBtn, page.html:521-523) do move the range, and #dateLabel (page.html:179-195) correctly renders a date (day view) or range (week view) heading, but the missing programmatic active-state marker fails the item.

items.item: Each booking shows its title or organiser and its start–end time as text, and its block covers exactly that stretch of the time axis (a 09:30–11:00 booking spans one and a half hours)
items.evidence: booking-block markup (page.html:255-259) renders title (`escapeHtml(b.title)`), time range (`fmtRange(b.startMin,b.endMin)`) and organizer as text. Position/height are computed from the same per-30-min ROW_H unit as the hour axis (`top:((b.startMin-DAY_START)/30)*ROW_H`, `height:((b.endMin-b.startMin)/30)*ROW_H-4`), so a 90-minute booking spans exactly 3 slots = 1.5× the 2-slot-per-hour spacing. Note: for 30-min bookings the 3 text lines can visually clip within the ~44px block (e.g. "Social Media Planning" in first.png), though the organizer text remains in the DOM.

items.item: Filters for minimum capacity and for equipment (such as projector or video conferencing) narrow the rooms listed, and the number of matching rooms is shown
items.evidence: No filter UI exists anywhere in the page — grep for 'filter'/'Capacity'/'Equipment' only matches the static ROOMS data and read-only capacity/equipment display strings (page.html:65-76, 227-233). There is no capacity input, equipment checkbox/select, or matching-room count.

items.item: Choosing a free slot opens a booking form already filled in with that room, date and start time
items.evidence: dayView click handler (page.html:528-533): `if(slot){ openBookingModal({ roomId: slot.dataset.room, date: slot.dataset.date, startMin: Number(slot.dataset.start) }); }`. openBookingModal() (page.html:349-357) pre-selects the matching `<option selected>` for room, sets `value="${date}"` on the date input, and pre-selects the start-time option.

items.item: Saving is blocked with an inline message when the time overlaps another booking of the same room (the message names that booking's time and organiser) or when the end is not after the start
items.evidence: handleBookingSubmit() (page.html:435-441) does block overlapping bookings inline: `showFormError('This room is already booked from '+fmtRange(conflict.startMin, conflict.endMin)+' ('+conflict.title+'). ...')` — but it names the conflicting booking's title, not its organiser, so the required organiser name is missing. There is also no explicit 'end not after start' check; the duration is restricted to a fixed positive-value dropdown (page.html:81-86) so that scenario is never validated or reachable.

items.item: Cancelling a booking asks for confirmation in a dialog that names the room, date and time and offers a way to keep the booking
items.evidence: Clicking 'Cancel Booking' replaces #cancelArea with 'Are you sure you want to cancel this booking?' plus 'Yes, Cancel' / 'Keep Booking' buttons (page.html:488-495), while the surrounding, still-visible modal content (room badge, title, `${dateLabel} · ${fmtRange(...)}` at page.html:467-475) continues to name the room, date and time for that same booking. denyCancel re-opens openDetailModal(id), keeping the booking.

items.item: Free slots and bookings are focusable buttons or links whose accessible names give the room, date, time and status (such as "Lotus room, Thu 5 Nov, 09:00–09:30, free"), not click handlers on bare divs
items.evidence: Both are plain, non-interactive `<div>` elements with click delegation only: `.slot-cell` (page.html:249, only a `title="Book ..."` tooltip attribute, no tabindex/role/aria-label) and `.booking-block` (page.html:255). Neither is a button/link, neither is keyboard-focusable, and neither exposes an accessible name describing room/date/time/status.

items.item: When no rooms match the filters, a message with a clear-filters action takes the place of the grid, and loading and error-with-retry states are built in
items.evidence: No filters exist (see capacity/equipment item), so there is no empty-state/clear-filters path, and no loading or error/retry UI appears anywhere in the markup or script (grep for 'retry'/'loading'/'Error' only matches booking-form validation messages like showFormError, page.html:427-453).

notes: This is a fairly 'real' bespoke calendar implementation (real SVG icons, functional date math, per-room color coding) rather than a generic dashboard template, so none of the listed template tells (greeting-header, kpi-icon-tiles, gradient, glass, emoji-icon, rainbow-status, sidebar-promo-card, etc.) clearly apply — no gradients/backdrop-blur/uppercase tracked labels/emoji were found in the markup. Main functional gaps are: room/time axis orientation is columns-not-rows, no aria active-view state, no capacity/equipment filtering (and thus no empty/loading/error states), conflict message omits the organiser, and slots/bookings are non-semantic, non-focusable divs. Audit.json also flags 7 text-contrast failures on booking-block subtext and a single-primary-action violation (both New Booking and the active Day/Week toggle are filled blue buttons).
